questions.text: Based on the passage, what does the author identify as the central challenge of modern urban planning?

comprehension.text: Modern cities face a paradox: as populations grow, the need for dense housing increases, yet high-rise living often strips away the very qualities that make urban life appealing — parks, street-level commerce, and a human scale of architecture. Urban planners must navigate this tension carefully, finding ways to increase capacity without sacrificing the neighbourhoods that attract residents in the first place.
